title: Adaptive governance: tag-based observability fences and operator audit trails
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Summary: Implement a tag-first governance layer for observability streams (traces, logs, metrics) that lets downstream pipelines apply enforcement (redaction, retention, routing) based on curated tags and an operator audit trail that records who, when, and why data policies were changed. This is intended to provide fine-grained policy application without heavy per-tenant schema changes and to make operator actions auditable for compliance reviews.

Goals:
- Introduce immutable tags attached to observability events at ingestion (origin tags + enrichment tags).
- Allow policy profiles to map tags to enforcement actions: soft-mask, field-strip, tiered-retention, or route-to-escrow.
- Record operator and automation policy changes in an audit trail with context (diff, rollout actor, rollback token).
- Provide a lightweight tracing hook so sampled traces carry tag provenance metadata for replay and debugging.
- Keep runtime overhead per-event <3% p99 latency impact at normal request sizes.

Acceptance criteria:
- Ingestion adaptor attaches at least three canonical tags (tenant_id_hash, env, pii_indicator) and supports custom enrichment rules by team.
- Policy engine can evaluate tag->action mappings and return enforcement decisions in <5ms median for common rule sets.
- Audit trail entries are immutable, include user id, timestamp, change diff, and a corresponding ticket/PR reference when applicable.
- End-to-end tests demonstrating redaction + retention applied to a synthetic tenant dataset, and ability to rehydrate escrowed artifacts under an approved workflow.
- Dashboard updates show policy evaluation latency and percent of events redacted per tag.

Design decisions and trade-offs:
- Tag-first vs schema-driven: We chose a tag-first model to avoid coupling governance to every telemetry schema change. Tags are less granular than full schema masking but provide flexible control and faster iteration for new policies.
- Deterministic pseudonymization: For tenant identifiers we will use tenant-salted HMACs (salt versioned per-tenant) rather than reversible encryption by default. This balances forensic needs and minimises key management complexity for most customers.
- Operator audit trail storage: Use an append-only, compressed ledger in the observability control-plane store with retention policy separate from telemetry retention. This keeps audit data compact and queryable for 2 years by default.
- Performance vs completeness: To meet latency targets we will perform enforcement decisions at a lightweight policy cache on the ingress path; full policy reasoning and longer-running transformations (e.g., deep NLP PII scans) are pushed to an async sanitization pipeline when configured.

Implementation plan:
1) Ingestion adaptor changes (traces/logs/metrics): add tag enrichment hooks and a small provenance header carrying tag versions.
2) Policy service: implement a tag->action evaluation API with in-memory LRU cache and versioned policy bundles.
3) Enforcement plugin: integrate into pipeline to apply masking/strip/route decisions; implement tiered retention lifecycles.
4) Audit trail service: append-only entries written on policy changes and on operator-initiated data reveals/unescrows.
5) Tracing hook: add optional trace annotations to sampled traces showing which policy rules were applied, for debugging regressions.
6) Telemetry/alerts: surface policy-eval latency, enforcement-rate, and number of operator reveals in Console dashboards.

Rollout plan:
- Canary rollout to non-prod tenants with flag enabled.
- Validation window with synthetic workloads to measure latency and correctness.
- Gradual enablement for low-risk customers, then broad rollout with an opt-in for async deep-scrub.

Metrics to monitor:
- Policy-eval p50/p95/p99 latency
- Percent of events with enforcement applied by tag
- Ingestion path p99 latency impact (target <3% relative)
- Operator reveal counts and time-to-audit-entry

Risks and mitigations:
- False negatives in tag assignment: provide fallback heuristics and an async scrub pipeline that can re-process missed events.
- Operator errors leading to overexposure: require 2-person reviews for production unescrow actions and log pre/post snapshots in the audit trail.
- Performance regressions: enforce strict perf budgets and CI perf tests that must pass before rollout.

Links and artifacts:
- Confluence: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/OBS/pages/Tag+Based+Governance+Design
- RFC PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rfcs/pull/214
- Ingest adaptor draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ingest/pull/872
- Policy service PoC: https://github.com/redwood-inference/policy/pull/19

Notes: This ticket covers the core infra and engineering work to attach tags, evaluate policies, and record operator audit events. Follow-ups will include a UX/Console story for policy editing, a standards doc for canonical tags, and a compliance connector for legal e-discovery requests.
